title: Mobile hand-off: a signed-out page navigation goes to the sign-in page, so the app never has to name the Console's login route
body:
Category: ③ a task the maintainer ordered directly.

Maintainer, 2026-11-04, in the session working on objectstack-ai/mobile#148, choosing how the app enters the mobile sign-in: "改成服务端入口".

Business reason: people on a provider that refuses embedded WebViews (Google among them) sign in through this flow, and an installed app stays in use for months. Today the app has to know the Console's sign-in route and how that page treats `redirect`. If a Console upgrade changes either one, those people are stranded on a page with no way back, and the app cannot detect it. 18.3.0 already showed this failure: the route shipped and the Console could not reach it (#29971). This flow has not shipped in any app yet, so the entry can change now with nothing to keep compatible.

Reader: `domain:server`, one PR on `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/one-time-token-handoff.ts`, with the spec docblock and the route ledger. objectstack-ai/mobile#190 then changes its entry URL.

Duplicate search: `"one-time-token/handoff"` in issues (4 hits) and `handoff "sign-in page" redirect anonymous` (5 hits). None asks for this.

## Today

The app opens `/_console/login?redirect=<hand-off>` in the system auth session (`signInEntryUrl` in objectstack-ai/mobile#190). `GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff` answers a missing or old session with `401` as raw JSON, so opening the route directly leaves the user looking at JSON.

## What changes

A page navigation to the hand-off with no session, or with a session older than five minutes, answers `302` to this deployment's Console sign-in page, with `redirect` set to the same hand-off request. After the sign-in, the page forwards back as #29971 specifies. The app then opens only the hand-off URL, a published route, and the sign-in route stays internal to this repository and its release.

Constraints:

1. **A non-navigation request still gets `401`.** The app's anonymous probe sends `Accept: application/json` and reads `401` as "this server registered me". Telling the two apart is a design question for the PR body: `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document` is the obvious signal, `Accept: text/html` the fallback. Neither has been measured in a real `ASWebAuthenticationSession` or Custom Tabs.
2. **Every refusal keeps its place, ahead of the new redirect.** `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` is judged first, then the closed query set, the registered scheme and the challenge. An invalid request gets `400` and never reaches the sign-in page.
3. **The browser stays on the origin the request arrived on.** The session cookie and #29979's same-origin match both depend on it. `AuthManager.getConsoleUrl` composes from the canonical origin, so a deployment reached on another host would move the browser. Say in the PR how `uiBasePath` is honoured without that move.
4. **`redirect` is rebuilt from the validated parameters**, root-relative under the deployment's base path, in the form `handoffNavigationTarget` in #29979 matches.
5. **It must not loop.** #29979 judges a session's age on the device's clock and this route judges it on the server's. On a device whose clock is behind, the page forwards a session the route calls old, and the route would send it straight back. Today that case stops on JSON; with this change it would bounce forever. This is read from the code, not measured. One way out: the route marks its redirect so the page keeps the form up until a sign-in happens on that page. That touches #29979, so agree it there.
6. **A deployment with no Console mounted.** Say what the route does there. It should not redirect to a page that does not exist.

## Security

This is a session-transfer flow, so the maintainer reviews and merges. Ruling A on #29714 stays as it is: a token is minted only for a session under five minutes old, and a cross-site navigation is refused. The new answer adds no capability, since anyone can already open `/_console/login?redirect=<hand-off>`.

## Acceptance notes

- Unit tests on `runOneTimeTokenHandoff`: page navigation with no session and with an old session gets the `302`; a JSON request gets `401`; an unregistered scheme, a bad challenge and an unknown parameter get `400` with no redirect; cross-site gets `400` first.
- Update the `Answers` list on `OneTimeTokenHandoffQuerySchema`, the route's module docblock, and its `auth-route-ledger.ts` note, which say "session required".
- An end-to-end browser test in this repository: open the hand-off signed out, sign in, and see the `302` to the registered scheme. It should run in CI, because it is what catches a Console upgrade breaking this for installed apps. It needs a registered scheme in the test server's config (#29972 is the `os serve` half).
- Say in the PR which release carries this. The app can only change its entry once this has shipped, because an older server answers the app's new entry with JSON.

Blocks: objectstack-ai/mobile#148
